findings.title: Public condition getters return unparenthesized OR/AND fragments
findings.body: `getFilterConditions()` returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses when only `eventTypeId` is set. `getAuthorizationConditions()` is also public, and for the user scope it returns `("userId" = ..) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)` unwrapped. `getBaseConditions` (lines 72-73) wraps both, so it is correct. A caller that composes the getters directly, e.g. ``WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}``, would get `a AND b OR c`. That binds as `(a AND b) OR c`, which lets the OR branch bypass the authorization condition. The only in-repo users of the getters are the tests, so nothing is broken today. Wrapping the returned fragments in parentheses, or making the getters private and exposing only `getBaseConditions`, would remove the trap. If you wrap them, update the test expectations to match.

findings.title: Public options type drops the scope/teamId discriminated union
findings.body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` allows `{scope: "team"}` without `teamId`, and allows any scope with an optional `teamId`. The constructor only catches this at runtime: `safeParse` fails and `options` becomes `null`, so authorization silently resolves to `1=0` (lines 62-63, 126-128). The failure is safe, but it is silent, and the compiler no longer catches the mistake. Keep `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the zod-inferred discriminated union) as the constructor parameter type, or express the public type as the same union, so a team scope without a `teamId` is a compile error.

findings.title: Tests only cover the new behavior through one happy-path query
findings.body: The Prisma.sql structure assertions compare generated SQL strings, so they mostly restate the implementation. The only test that runs the SQL against the database is `getBaseConditions` (lines 437-491), and it uses a single scope. The raw SQL for the org scope, the team scope, the `= ANY(array)` parameters, and the empty `userIdsFromOrg` / `userIdsFromTeam` branches that this PR adds are never executed. The fallthrough to a single `teamId` condition when there are no member user ids is untested. Add an executed query for the org and team scopes. Add one case where the team has no members, checking that the result is valid SQL and returns only team bookings.

contracts.action: Authorization and filter conditions are now built as Prisma.Sql raw fragments instead of Prisma where-inputs. A new `getBaseConditions` replaces `findMany`.
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous `findMany` combined `AND: [auth, filter]` into a Prisma findMany on bookingTimeStatusDenormalized. The new path returns a Sql fragment for callers to embed in `$queryRaw`.
contracts.before_after: Before: the Prisma client quoted identifiers and parameterised values, and the combined where was applied inside findMany. After: column names are hard-coded quoted identifiers that I checked against the schema.prisma view (userId, teamId, eventTypeId, eventParentId, isTeamBooking). Values are bound as parameters through Prisma.sql, so there is no injection path. Arrays use `= ANY(${array})`, and the same idiom is used in PermissionRepository. Authorization is checked in the same way as before (org owner/admin membership), and a fallback to `1=0` replaces `{id:-1}`. A grep of the packages found no other callers of `findMany`, so nothing is left calling the removed method.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change in this part. The conditions feed Insights booking queries in later or other code. The only in-repo consumer is the integration test.
contracts.failure_mode: If the options fail zod validation, or the user is not an org owner/admin, the condition is `1=0` and no rows are returned. This is a safe failure, but a silent one. A DB rejection on the repository lookups propagates to the caller. Combining auth and filter parenthesises both sides, so authorization cannot be bypassed through getBaseConditions.

summary: The raw-SQL conversion of InsightsBookingService is correct as far as I could verify. The column names match the view, values are bound as parameters, and `getBaseConditions` parenthesises both sides so authorization is not bypassed. I have three non-blocking points. The public getters return unparenthesized OR/AND fragments. The new public options type loses the discriminated union, so a team scope without a `teamId` is no longer a compile error. The raw SQL for the org and team scopes is never run against the database in the tests.
